title: What is Next.js?
description: Understand the problems Next.js solves and why it's the React framework for production.

slides.title: The Web Before Next.js 🌐
slides.content:
# The Old Way

In a **plain React** app, everything happens in the browser.

* The server sends an almost empty HTML file.
* JavaScript loads and then renders the whole page (Client‑Side Rendering).
* This is slow for users and bad for SEO.

Imagine a restaurant where the chef only starts cooking **after** you sit down. 🍳

slides.title: Meet Next.js – The Production React Framework ⚛️
slides.content:
# Next.js Superpowers

Next.js adds crucial features on top of React:

* **Server‑Side Rendering (SSR)** – HTML is generated on the server, so users see content faster.
* **Static Site Generation (SSG)** – Pages can be pre‑built at build time for instant loading.
* **File‑system Routing** – Create a file, get a route. No router setup needed.
* **API Routes** – Write backend code right inside your Next.js app.
* **Image Optimisation, Fonts, Metadata** – Built‑in performance and SEO tools.

quizData.question: What is the main rendering issue with plain React apps?

options.text: Slow initial load because JavaScript must render everything

quizData.explanation: Plain React uses Client‑Side Rendering: the browser must download, parse, and run JS before any content appears. Next.js pre‑renders HTML on the server.

slides.title: How Next.js Pre‑renders 🖨️
slides.content:
# Two Forms of Pre‑rendering

Next.js can generate HTML in two ways:

1. **Static Generation (SSG)** – HTML is generated **at build time**. Ideal for blogs, marketing pages.
2. **Server‑Side Rendering (SSR)** – HTML is generated **on each request**. Perfect for dashboards, user‑specific data.

Both give you **fully rendered HTML** before JavaScript even loads. Then React *hydrates* the page to make it interactive.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Hydration Analogy

Pre‑rendering gives you a dry sponge (static HTML). Hydration adds water (JavaScript event listeners) so it becomes a functional sponge. 🧽

quizData.question: When should you use Static Generation (SSG)?

options.text: When the page content changes on every request
When the page content can be pre-built and is the same for all users
When you need a database query for each visitor
When you don’t care about performance

quizData.explanation: SSG is perfect for pages like blogs or product listings that can be generated once at build time and reused for all users.

slides.title: The Big Picture 🖼️
slides.content:
# Next.js is the Full Package

* **Frontend**: React components (JSX, hooks, state).
* **Backend**: API routes, server‑side logic.
* **Build system**: Webpack/Turbopack, auto‑optimised.
* **Deployment**: One‑click deploy to Vercel, or any Node.js host.

It’s like getting a fully equipped kitchen, not just a stove.
